The game is not beginner friendly, far from it. Everything also takes so much time to make, not for those who can't wait, literally days of waiting. Aside from that, nearly everything is obtainable, the community is very active when it comes to trading it has become a meme. And also so much grinding and even more waiting to get every stuff.

Enemies are also extremely powerful at steel path mode, even more when they reach level 9999 maximum level during a mission. Its all about understanding how mods work and how countless unique mechanics of every weapons/warframe synergize with each other.

Any warframe/weapon is viable against high level enemies, its all about how much you will invest in them to make it work. Also the game isn't just about looting, it has too much content. Definitely not beginner friendly.

10/10. Free to play, impossible to understand, financially dangerous if you discover the cosmetics.

Overall, the game is fine. I found myself actually quite enjoying the story, for what it's worth it's pretty entertaining. The F2P aspects of the game are plentifull but my main problem with this game is the grind. It's ridiculous. I'm not one to ussualy complain about a grind but this game takes it to another extreme. Every single little mechanic in this game in some way shape or form boils back down to some sort of timer or meaningless grind. Every item you make, or components for items, takes a day if not more. Now in the meantime you can keep playing, sure, but that also is limited behind a grind. Wether it's the mastery level which needs leveling, or an item you first grind towards all day, and then still have to wait about 4 days before you can actually use it. IF you want to make every cool looking frame in the game? or every weapon? Too bad, you're out of slots. Which you NEED plattinum for. Now platinum can technically be achieved F2P but it's so painfully slow if you don't have any high level friends to taxi you into higher level relic missions it's insane. Overall, if you're like me and you're looking for something fun to play and maybe for free, it'll be fun. For about a week, but after you realize the ammount of time that's needed to achieve anything it'll feel more like a task than a fun time.

First played on PS4 back in 2018. This was my go to game for years until around Angels of Zariman, when the PS4 started to really struggle. The constant disconnects made the game unplayable.

Then cross save came out and on day two of getting back into things I lost 3 gold drops from a endless relic mission on, you guessed it, the Zariman (I have an irrational distaste for that area of the game now). Dropped it again for about a year.

Finally started playing again back in late 2024. Why? Because it is one of the best games ever made.

The movement is lighting fast and buttery smooth. The different playable Warframes each have a unique look, playstyle, and lore. The level of customization is incredibly deep in both in terms of build-crafting and aesthetic appearance. The music, gameplay, and story are all top tier.

I've been playing this game off and on for almost a decade now and I can still count the number of bad interactions I've had with other players on my hands. The only other game I've played with as welcoming a community as this one is Deep Rock Galactic.

The developers really care about making the game as enjoyable as possible, and to prove that, they play it themselves. I don't mean they play one choreographed level to showcase something; I mean they actively play the game with people from the community live on stream, as well as on their time off. They love this game, and it makes the players love them all the more.

Does the game have problems? Of course. Is the early part of the game thin on story? Yes. Does the game do a great job of explaining how to play it? Not really. Can the networking be buggy? Certainly. Is RNG the bane of my existence? You betcha.

None of that should stop you from trying the game though. This game is easily the best live service game out there, and it's free. If you haven't played it yet, do yourself a favor and give it a try. Hop in the Q&A chat and ask questions. Join a clan. Do your quests. There is something in this game for everyone. What do you have to lose?

I've been playing Warframe since mid-2024. Overall, I see many flaws of the game, but for every flaw there are 20 compliments I could give to the game. However, I am sure there are many general reviews that say "DE has lost the plot" or "DE is great" but neither review tells a story with enough depth. I want to be clear here and now that Warframe is worth your time and is fun. Admittedly, for people who are like me (someone who is familiar with looter-shooters) I think Warframe's biggest flaw at attracting players is a lack of a good in-game tutorial and early game pacing. Also, I'll admit most of my hours are inflated as for leaving the game open. I have less than half of my hours.
That being said I noticed recently (as in 2026 leading up to TAU) that Warframe has had admittedly bad update launches consistently. I think DE does need to be criticized for not delaying updates as a whole when they need it clearly. It feels all so disappointing to see a Warframe update come out and know its an aggravating experience the first few days sometimes, as the first half of the year has felt like that. I believe Icebind the new 6 player gamemode is a  fantastic addition that needs tweaks and adjustments but overall is pretty great. 
At the time of this review I have done 3 runs and got most of the side objectives as something I needed to do. I can see the frustration of this gamemode being that you are reliant on randoms, but many of the side objectives are incredibly intuitive that they can be done the first time you see them and require no knowledge before hand. I think ultimately that should be the goal for a gamemode like this as if the side objectives are too demanding I fear that KWTD for Icebind will become too common. A lot of complaints about this gamemode I believe are unwarranted as they tend to say the mode is unfun and feels too random, but the complaints about the loot are more than justified as truthfully the side objectives have a good chance to give meager scraps for loot. I trust the developers will continue to add to this mode as from the grand-scheme of Warframe the mode is admittedly not finished due to their not being enough variety and different gamemodes do not feel balanced as survival and disruption seem to be the best modes to pick. As a whole I believe the issue for many players with Icebind is that it forces you to have builds geared at such a high level of game-play that many are not familiar with as it felt like the enemies were tougher than level cap runs in my experience: granted that is impart due to the modifiers. As a whole this is a significant upgrade from Archimedea.
To address that "DE has lost the plot" in relation to how Warframe's story has been expanding, Warframe has never had a more clear vision than it does now. Keep in mind that I only saw Warframe's story from playing it in a few months or so and missed out on some FOMO events for story telling, but nevertheless there are many great videos that showcased that Warframe has always had a messy story that would change on the whim's of the previous developer team. While I have only played what Rebecca's team has been producing they're storytelling has been far more clear and consistent, but Warframe has never been a story driven game. Warframe is as fun as it is due to it being a sandbox for gameplay and fashion. Fashion framing is a serious task in Warframe as well as build crafting. That is what Warframe has been primarily about from my experience and DE keeps releasing massive changes to the game that shake-up these aspects and add so much variety to build-crafting. For example, Riven Splicers from Icebind allow many primary weapons to achieve 100% ammo efficiency. And a lot of new fashion choices with Ephmeras, SIgnas, and Sigils being expanded out far more than before. This is to say at the core Warframe is making the adjustments it needs to. While I don't think Warframe is particularly good at storytelling and I would say it is similar to Destiny in that regard, Warframe knows what changes it needs to make mostly and it doing so.

It's free, your going to see that a lot. By now you likely have at least heard of this game. I played it when it came out, didn't like it, didn't understand it. Tried a few more times and eventually started to enjoy it. Bullet jumping and slicing people in half with my space mom was alright. I started to understand the mechanics and with google was able to figure my way through most of the game solo, but there are massive catches and that's why I'm not recommending it. Yes, it's a completely free game, but...not really. Yes it's entertaining for a bit if this is your type of game, but each persons mileage is going to vary. 

First the story. I love a good story, or even a bad one and I enjoyed Warframes, but I started to notice the plot was chunky. Start a story and not really understand what's going on, and then end it with no after care for the next chunk. Turns out that a lot of story telling happened through in game limited time events. So that mean it's gone. Get your butt to youtube to watch a breakdown video because sorry chump, you didn't play the game during this time so no story for you. The reasoning behind this design is crap, and if they spent even half as much time trying to make a cohesive narrative as they spend trying to milk your wallet they could easily fix this problem. They don't want to. Some people won't care. If your just here to slash mobs and farm materials then in you go, your going to have a great time, but if you care about story at all this is putrid design and shows a lack of interest in the consumer in such a way that killed any interest I had in the game. 

Sunsetting and premium. Apparently most everything that was in the game at any time can be gotten again. There are apparently a few warframes that are permanently gone which means they do in fact remove things from the game, but even if you want to be charitable the system they have in place is sunsetting light. The big play is to vault warframes and gear and no longer provide a set in game path to acquire these items. How do you get around this? Well give them money for platinum, and then go to the Warframe ebay-like website that is not affiliated with them and trade other players for their crap. Huzzah. See something in the shop that isn't available anymore, or is rare, if its a warframe you better hope you have the cash because a single warframe costs 20 dollars for their premium currency exchange. Just getting started? Start actually enjoying the game and getting stuff to build weapons and warframes...too bad. Inventory is full. Pay up kiddo. You want more than three warframes or like ten weapons, well open up that wallet. What's that? The only way to get better stuff is by leveling up your mastery which means leveling a bunch of warframes and weapons on repeat, and some of those weapons and warframes are needed for later so selling it is a huge trap? Oh well, platinum please. 

Gameplay loop. This one is more of a pet peeve of mine, but it's found in this game so I'll mention it if you happen to share my view. Games like Warframe, Diablo, POE. They don't show you how to play it. They give you a game to play, but that isn't the game. The game is dungeons, and specific grinding. Everything is hella complicated and in my opinion, complicated for the sake of being complicated. They could just as easily keep things simple while keeping their nested systems and in universe language. It doesn't make you smart for googling how to make a key to enter into a dungeon to grind the materials you need. You could just keep it simple and cut out the middle man of googling it and get the same return. I'll add onto this for this game they add a bunch of modes. You like the warframe mode? Well I hope you like not playing it sometimes. You have a darks souls like, a space shooter, a normal guy with low resources mode and probably more besides I haven't unlocked yet. That's kind of cool to me honestly, except every time I have played these modes I spend a good amount of time being annoyed, and I know I can't be the only one. Do a mission as your low resource guy and spend twenty minutes fighting your resource regeneration. Destroy this object, you have 100 energy. That object takes 50 energy to destroy, there are three of them, so enjoy waiting watching your bar recoup...it's that level of bad design where it feels malicious rather than accidental. 

Overall. I don't recommend this game unless your willing to be honest with yourself about it, which I'm learning from my own issues is not as easy as it sounds. This is an MMO and has all the same MMO trappings of timed and limited stuff. It's free to play which means that there is heavy emphasis on getting your money even if the community swears up and down that it's not that bad. It isn't, but you just got to be willing to not get what you want sometimes for the sole reason they want you to pay money for your happiness. If you care about the story you might get frustrated. It's not a masterpiece, but it's present enough to be interesting and their mangling of it is purposeful and strange. So if your okay with all of that and you just want to slice dudes in half and parkour around maps then I recommend it highly.  The gameplay loop is fun. Bullet jumping and parkour are legitimately easy and fun. I could never bunny hop in counter strike, this takes all the skill out and makes it a simple and fun experience for all. Don't be sucked in because it's free. People lose their minds when they see the free tag and are not objective about their experience at all. The good news is there is no barrier to entry, try it, see if you like the movement, the gameplay, and find out for yourself.
